Today I had the honour of attending an event where @vstoronto announced the expansion of the Ask for Angela initiative across the GTA. 

If you need support and are experiencing domestic violence you can ask a trained staff member at participating locations, “Is Angela here?” or “Is Angela working today?” or you can ask in any way that feels natural to you. 

Staff are trained to recognize the request & respond calmly & safely. They will immediately & discreetly bring you to a safe space & help connect you to the support you need.

Founded in partnership with Loblaw Companies Limited, the program is expanding across stores in the GTA, creating more safe places where someone can quietly ask for help & be met with the care & understanding they deserve.

If you or someone you know needs immediate support, Victim Services Toronto is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, their 24-Hour Crisis Line is 416-808-7066.

caption:
No matter how many of these posts I write, they never get easier. The tears flow the same, the ache is still felt deep within your heart.

Even as I write this I don’t want to share because maybe if I don’t, it won’t be true. But sadly I’m faced with the reality of our family losing yet another loved one.

Our family lost my father in law, Len Farinacci, or as I called him ever since I had the honour witnessing him become one - Grandpa.

As I go through messages from my FIL, a couple things are consistent through every message. Love, & not surface level love, BIG love. He loved with conviction. His ‘love you’ messages read louder somehow than the love you’s I received in messages from others.

Gratitude. Nearly every message expressed gratitude. Whether it be gratitude for the beautiful day he had, or gratitude for the day that was coming, he expressed a deep level of gratitude. He’d express thanks for simply sharing with him about the day his grandkids had, or an invitation to a birthday or dinner. Even in photos of sunsets or plants he sent me he’d always express gratitude for the gift of how they made him feel. He’d express thanks for the small things in life, moments or things that most wouldn’t take the time to see let alone appreciate.

Pride. This man felt pride. He was proud beyond words of each of his 5 kids & his grandchildren. He felt pride for the big & the little things. He wore it on his face with a smile grinning from cheek to cheek & excitement in his voice. 

Regret is the biggest & darkest thief in the aftermath of death, this I know to be true, however I will share that I wish I had said this to him while he was still here so that he could have felt the same love, gratitude & pride he filled my life with - thank you for filling our lives with so much love. Thank you for teaching us the importance of family. And most importantly thank you for the gift of your first son, the love of my life, for teaching him to love deeply & to care for his family just the way that you did.

I hope heaven is as beautiful as we talked about it being & that your wine glass is full with your favourite vintage.

Cheers to you Grandpa, we will miss you dearly.

caption:
Happy Heavenly Birthday Baby Bro

Today you would have turned 39.
One more year passes without you here.
Another set of candles not lit.
Frozen in time forever young.

I miss the way you sound. I find myself playing your voice texts over & over just to get a glimpse of a time when you were still here. 
Carefully playing them, afraid I’ll accidentally delete one and lose that connection to you forever.

I stare at your photo in our house, I don’t just look, I stare at them. There’s something about photos of you that feel real. They still have life to them.
Maybe it’s your eyes, they have a light shining in them that makes it feel as if you are still right here with us.

There are no more phone calls to make to uncle clinton (aka uncle woody) to wish you a happy birthday. So instead we gather around the table, make a special dinner and cheers our glasses. And our birthday wish for you, that’s simple, we wish you were still here.

Today is your birthday and I refuse to let today be just another day because it’s more than that. Without today being your birthday we wouldn’t know what this deep meaning of love is. caption:
I FINALLY decided!

We’re six months into 2026, so I thought this was the perfect time to FINALLY decide on my word of the year. Ya, it only took me 6 months to claim my word.

CREATE

If I’m being honest, I originally wanted the word Create to be my word, but I thought it didn’t feel BIG enough. It felt like I was playing small, which is funny because I really just wasn’t leaning into it as much as I needed to. I was the one playing small with what I thought it had to mean. 

I was getting in the way of what my intuition was telling me. 

My original word of the year wasn’t even a word, it was a phrase. A good phrase, but not one that would serve me this year.

When the word Create first came to me while on our family vacation in Mexico, I curled my nose at it. I thought “Create? Create what? Crafts?” - I mean, I’m here for all the crafting, but I didn’t get how this was going to be my word for the year.

And then. I got it. It hit me.

Create healing

Create space

Create love

Create balance

Create time

Create impact

Create the life I want

Create dreams into reality

And yes, Create beautiful pieces with my hands.

My intuition was right. It was leading me to what I’ve needed.

Creating with my hands has been a HUGE part of this year. It was while creating a craft that I realized Create was the word all along, I just needed my mind to catch up to what my soul had already called me to do. Creating with my hands is what has brought me healing and continues to do so. 

Sometimes we have to get out of our own way and listen to our intuition. 

So, yes, Create is more than just creating with my hands, it’s also creating with intention.

Here I am, with under 6 months left to the year, to tell you: my word is Create.

And you can create what you want for the last 6 months of 2026, too.

caption:
Keeping my grandmas traditions going

I didn’t stress about baking this holiday season but you better believe I made sure I made my Nannies Nuts and Bolts recipe!

Ive been enjoying this recipe since I was little and will continue making this for my family in my grandmas honour. 

This year I packed 3 tins up and treated our flight attendants on our flight down to Mexico with them and when I tell you that each of the flight attendants came over and thanked us for their special treats and RAVED about them, I mean they RAVED about them! It made my heart so happy to share with them that the recipe is my grandmas. 

My brothers used to say not to share my Nannies recipe but to me the more people making her recipe and enjoying it - the better!! That’s just more people keeping her memory alive and keeping her beautiful Christmas tradition going!!

This recipe is a double recipe:
Nannie Laura’s Nuts n Bolts
2 boxes of cheerios
2 boxes of rice Chex
2 boxes of corn Chex
2 bags of pretzels (the size of the bag in the video)
4 tins of cashews (or the large tub in video)
2 bottles of peanuts (shown in video)
2 lbs butter melted
6 tbsps of Worcestershire
6 tsps celery salt
6 tsps Garlic powder
6 tsps Onion salt
2 tsps tobacco 
6 tsps paprika 

Mix cereals, pretzels and nuts in large pans
Melt butter and mix in spices and pour all over cereal mixture and stir.

Place in a oven heated at 250 degress for one hour.
Every 15 minutes take pans out and stir.

Happy sharing this recipe as long as you speak my sweet Nannies name when you share it with others ♥️

Merry Christmas!! xo
